title: Ajj Zulf Sanwari Jani Ae
titleEnglish: Today the Tresses Will Be Combed
subtitle: A collection of Punjabi ghazals
author: Dr. Muhammad Ahmad Tabassum
editor: M.A. Azad Khokhar, Gojra (revised and arranged)
price: A prayer for the author's soul (isaal-e-sawab)
place: Gojra, District Toba Tek Singh, Punjab, Pakistan
about: Dr. Muhammad Ahmad Tabassum was a doctor and poet from Gojra, in Pakistan's Punjab. He wrote in Punjabi, his mother tongue, and sometimes in Urdu. His friends remembered him for his warmth, his love of poetry gatherings, and his poems in praise of the Prophet. After he died, his daughter Saeeda Akhtar gathered his scattered poems, and his friend M.A. Azad Khokhar arranged them into this book. It was published in 2016. Instead of a price, the book asks readers for one thing: a prayer for the poet's soul.

dedication.original: غزل شائقین واسطے اپنی ماں بولی پنجابی وچ لکھیا گیا پنجابی غزل پراگا دوستاں سجناں متراں دی دلجوئی تے اہناں دی منگ دے مطابق پیش اے۔ مینوں دوستاں مہرباناں دی محبت پیار لگن تے پکا یقین اے کہ اوہ ایس پنجابی غزل پراگے نوں اپنی سوچ شوق دے مطابق پسند فرمان گے تے دوجے دوستاں نوں پڑھن تے مطالعہ دی دعوت دین گے۔ ایہہ کتاب یقیناً پنجابی ادب اندر خوبصورت وادھے دا سبب بنے گی تے ڈاکٹر علیہ رحمۃ دی یاد نوں زندہ رکھے گی۔
dedication.translation: This collection of Punjabi ghazals, written in our mother tongue for those who love the ghazal, is offered to comfort friends and loved ones, as they asked. I am sure that friends, out of their love, will enjoy it in their own way and invite others to read it. This book will surely add something beautiful to Punjabi literature and keep alive the memory of the Doctor, may God have mercy on him.
dedication.story: The book opens with a short note from the poet's friend, Azad Khokhar. He explains that these poems were collected because friends asked for them. He hopes people will enjoy them and pass them on. Most of all, he hopes the book will keep his friend's memory alive.

notes: The printed contact phone numbers on page 2 are left out on purpose.
Page 3 (first half of the contents) was only partly photographed. The contents list is rebuilt from the poems.
